query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to produce the improvement, a measurable outcome relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with clear observations that would falsify it.

revised_generation.hypothesis: High-entropy alloys treated with grain refinement will exhibit improved hardness and strength without sacrificing useful mechanical performance
revised_generation.uncertainty: Limited data on long-term performance and the effect of grain refinement on high-entropy alloys
revised_generation.falsification_experiment: Comparison of treated and untreated alloys under standard testing protocols, with measurements of hardness, strength, and microstructure
